name: Everyday communication
question: When plans change, what would you like to hear from each other?
perspectives: A quick heads-up helps me rearrange my evening.
I like to have a new plan ready before I reach out.
agreement: Send a short heads-up first. Work out the new plan together when you have the details.
checkIn: Did the early heads-up help? Did you both have enough information to plan your evening?

name: Conflict and repair
question: If either of you needs a break during an argument, how will you know when to come back?
perspectives: I can take a break if I know we'll finish the conversation.
I need a little quiet before I can listen again.
agreement: Either person can ask for a pause. Pick a time to come back before you step away.
checkIn: Was the break long enough? Was it easy to start the conversation again?

name: Support and closeness
question: What feels supportive at the end of a hard day?
perspectives: I feel close when someone listens before offering ideas.
Taking a task off someone's plate is how I show I care.
agreement: Ask whether listening, a little space, or practical help would feel good today.
checkIn: Which kind of support did you welcome? What would you ask for next time?

name: Shared priorities
question: What would each of you like to protect time for this week?
perspectives: I would love an evening together without other plans.
I need some time to myself to recharge after work.
agreement: Choose one evening to spend together and set aside personal time that each person can count on.
checkIn: Did both of you get the time you needed? What would you change for next week?
